examples_0305

Consider the following product of linear binomials:

\[({8}x+{9})({-9}x+{1})\]

When the expression is expanded and like terms are combined, an equivalent expression can be expressed in standard form:

\[ax^2+bx+c\]

where \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\) are integers.

  • What is the value of \(b\)?

You could use the box method.


Or, you can FOIL...


Either way, you should first get \[{-72}x^{2}+{8}x-{81}x+{9}\]

And, after combining like terms, you should get \[{-72}x^{2}-{73}x+{9}\]

Thus, \(a=-72\) and \(b=-73\) and \(c=9\). This question specifically asked for the value of \(b\), so the answer is \(-73\).

Consider the following product of linear binomials:

\[({7}x+{9})(x-{8})\]

When the expression is expanded and like terms are combined, an equivalent expression can be expressed in standard form:

\[ax^2+bx+c\]

where \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\) are integers.

  • What is the value of \(b\)?

You could use the box method.


Or, you can FOIL...


Either way, you should first get \[{7}x^{2}-{56}x+{9}x-{72}\]

And, after combining like terms, you should get \[{7}x^{2}-{47}x-{72}\]

Thus, \(a=7\) and \(b=-47\) and \(c=-72\). This question specifically asked for the value of \(b\), so the answer is \(-47\).

When the expression is expanded and like terms are combined, an equivalent expression can be expressed in standard form:

\[ax^2+bx+c\]

where \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\) are integers.

You could use the box method.


Or, you can FOIL...


Either way, you should first get \[{-45}x^{2}-{10}x+{18}x+{4}\]

Thus, \(a=-45\) and \(b=8\) and \(c=4\). This question specifically asked for the value of \(b\), so the answer is \(8\).

The product of a linear polynomial times a quadratic polynomial is a cubic polynomial. Let \(r(x)\) represent the product of the linear binomial and the quadratic trinomial shown below.

\[r(x)~~=~~\left({7}x+{6}\right) \cdot \left({-2}x^{2}+{4}x+{7}\right)\]

The resulting cubic polynomial can be expressed in standard form.

\[r(x)~=~ax^3+bx^2+cx+d\]

Identify the coefficients \(a\), \(b\), \(c\), and \(d\).

  • \(a=\)
  • \(b=\)
  • \(c=\)
  • \(d=\)
* \(7x\) \(6\)
\(-2x^2\) \(-14x^3\) \(-12x^2\)
\(4x\) \(28x^2\) \(24x\)
\(7\) \(49x\) \(42\)

\[r(x)~~=~~ {-14}x^{3}+{28}x^{2}+{49}x-{12}x^{2}+{24}x+{42}\]

Combine like terms.

\[r(x)~~=~~ {-14}x^{3}+{16}x^{2}+{73}x+{42}\]

So,

  • \(a=-14\)
  • \(b=16\)
  • \(c=73\)
  • \(d=42\)

The product of a linear polynomial times a quadratic polynomial is a cubic polynomial. Let \(r(x)\) represent the product of the linear binomial and the quadratic trinomial shown below.

\[r(x)~~=~~\left({-9}x+{3}\right) \cdot \left({6}x^{2}+{7}x-{5}\right)\]

The resulting cubic polynomial can be expressed in standard form.

\[r(x)~=~ax^3+bx^2+cx+d\]

Identify the coefficients \(a\), \(b\), \(c\), and \(d\).

  • \(a=\)
  • \(b=\)
  • \(c=\)
  • \(d=\)
* \(-9x\) \(3\)
\(6x^2\) \(-54x^3\) \(18x^2\)
\(7x\) \(-63x^2\) \(21x\)
\(-5\) \(45x\) \(-15\)

\[r(x)~~=~~ {-54}x^{3}-{63}x^{2}+{45}x+{18}x^{2}+{21}x-{15}\]

Combine like terms.

\[r(x)~~=~~ {-54}x^{3}-{45}x^{2}+{66}x-{15}\]

So,

  • \(a=-54\)
  • \(b=-45\)
  • \(c=66\)
  • \(d=-15\)

\(-1x^2\) \(5x^3\) \(2x^2\)
\(-6x\) \(30x^2\) \(12x\)
\(-7\) \(35x\) \(14\)

\[r(x)~~=~~ {5}x^{3}+{30}x^{2}+{35}x+{2}x^{2}+{12}x+{14}\]

  • \(b=\)
  • \(c=\)
  • \(d=\)

\(2x^2\) \(-2x^3\) \(-18x^2\)
\(3x\) \(-3x^2\) \(-27x\)
\(8\) \(-8x\) \(-72\)

\[r(x)~~=~~ {-2}x^{3}-{3}x^{2}-{8}x-{18}x^{2}-{27}x-{72}\]
